title: The Silent Login Shell
description: Login shells skip .bashrc because .profile never sources it; wire them together and prove APP_MODE survives a login shell.
scenario: Your custom environment works in terminal tabs but evaporates over SSH. Reason: SSH starts a LOGIN shell, which reads ~/.profile — and this .profile is empty, so ~/.bashrc (where APP_MODE=training and the team aliases live) is never sourced. Fix /home/intern/.profile so it sources ~/.bashrc for bash users, then prove a login shell sees APP_MODE.
symptoms: Over SSH: `echo $APP_MODE` prints nothing, aliases are gone
In local terminal tabs everything works (they start non-login shells)
mission: Make /home/intern/.profile source /home/intern/.bashrc (guarded for bash), so that `bash -lc 'echo $APP_MODE'` prints training.

hints.title: Two kinds of shells
hints.content: Login shells (SSH, console, bash -l) read ~/.profile; non-login interactive shells (terminal tabs) read ~/.bashrc. Ubuntu wires them together FROM .profile — and that wiring is missing here.

hints.title: The standard guard
hints.content: `[ -n "$BASH_VERSION" ] && . "$HOME/.bashrc"` sources .bashrc only under bash (sh/dash would choke on bashisms).

hints.title: Prove it
hints.content: `bash -l` starts a login shell: it reads .profile → sources .bashrc → APP_MODE must appear.
